$comment: Copy to ./odw.config.json, ~/.config/odw/config.json, or pass --config. All keys are TOP-LEVEL (no 'settings' wrapper; odw warns about unknown or misplaced keys). odw never calls model APIs directly: each adapter is a local CLI it shells out to. The nine below ship as built-ins, so you only need this file to change defaults, tune flags, or add your own adapter.
//stallTimeout: ODW extension. Seconds an agent may print nothing on stdout or stderr before it is killed (like a timeout) and restarted, at most stallRestarts times per agent call; null (the default) turns the watchdog off. It stays off for every built-in adapter because some CLIs (gemini, qwen, kimi in text mode) print nothing until they finish: enable it for adapters that stream progress — claude (stream-json: an event per turn), kilo, opencode — with a value above the longest single tool call. An adapter's own "stallTimeout" overrides this value; 0 turns the watchdog off for that adapter.
//transientRetries: ODW extension. A failed agent is classified from its CLI's exit status and output: rate_limit, quota, auth, timeout, stalled, not_found, permission or exit. A rate-limited one is run again after a backoff (the retry-after its CLI printed, else 15s doubling per retry, plus up to 20% jitter), at most transientRetries times per agent call and never waiting more than maxBackoff seconds at once. A spent quota or a failed login is never retried: its error says what to do, and the run goes on. An adapter's own "failures" patterns (regular expressions per class: rate_limit, quota, auth) are matched before the built-in table.
//worktreeSetup: ODW extension. A command run in every new isolated worktree (agent(…, { isolation: "worktree" })) once .worktreeinclude has brought files in, before the agent starts: a string runs through the platform shell, an array as an argv without one. It runs in the agent's workspace with ODW_RUN_ID, ODW_AGENT_ID and ODW_PORT set, and is killed after worktreeSetupTimeout seconds; one that fails or times out fails that agent (not the run), quoting the end of its output. null (the default) runs nothing.
//portRange: ODW extension. Every agent process gets ODW_PORT: a port from this inclusive range that no other running agent of the run holds (ports something already listens on are passed over), kept until its call settles, so a workflow can say "start your dev server on $ODW_PORT". Keep the range wider than concurrency.
//fanOutWarn: ODW extension. When one parallel() or pipeline() call fans out more than this many tasks or items, the run logs one warning with the count (it never blocks); 0 or null turns it off. What a run spends — tokens and cost as adapters report them (the built-in claude does), else output tokens estimated as chars/4 — shows in odw status, the live view and the dashboard.
//adaptiveConcurrency: ODW extension. An adapter's own "concurrency" (my_wrapper below sets 2) caps how many of its agents run at once, inside the run-wide concurrency (an agent needs a slot in both; each adapter queues first come, first served, and a throttled adapter never holds up the others). With adaptiveConcurrency, a rate limit halves its adapter's cap — that of an adapter without one starts at the run-wide cap — for the rest of the run, never below 1, and each minute without another gives one slot back; both are logged. false keeps every cap fixed. odw doctor and odw run's start banner show the caps.
//staggerFanOut: ODW extension. On adapters that declare "promptCache": true (the built-in claude does), one parallel() or pipeline() call whose agents' prompts share at least their first 1024 characters starts `first` of them, and the rest once the first one's CLI has produced output or delayMs later, whichever is sooner — so they read the prefix from the prompt cache instead of each paying for it. A lone agent, an agent with a shorter or different prompt, and a replayed one never wait; a stop ends the wait at once; each staggered fan-out logs one line. false or null turns it off.
//maxDiffBytes: ODW extension. An agent that runs with isolation: "worktree" leaves what it changed as a unified diff in the run directory (agents/<agentId>.diff): odw diff prints it, odw apply applies it, and the dashboard's Changes tab shows it. Past maxDiffBytes the diff keeps its head, cut at a line, and a note; its counts still describe the whole change. keepBranches also commits every isolated agent's change to a branch odw/<runId>/<agentId>-<label> of the source repository (keep: true does that for one agent; keep: false opts one out).
//maxTranscriptBytes: ODW extension. While each agent runs, what its CLI prints is kept in the run directory as its transcript: agents/<agentId>.transcript.jsonl (a JSONL adapter's events as received, other adapters' output as text lines) and agents/<agentId>.stderr.txt (the end of its stderr). odw logs <run> --agent <id|label> prints it readably (--raw as kept, --follow while it runs). Past maxTranscriptBytes per agent one truncation line ends it; 0 keeps no transcripts.
//permissions: ODW extension. What the run's agents may do: "read" (look, never edit or run commands — for research and review fan-outs), "edit" (the default: what every built-in always ran with) or "full" (no sandbox, no approvals). odw run|rerun|resume --permissions overrides it per run; an adapter's own "permissions" and an agent()'s { permissions } may only lower it. Each adapter's flags per tier are its "permissionArgs", spliced where its command has "{permission_args}". An agent that asks a CLI with no read flags for "read" fails before it starts; one that asks for "full" where the CLI declares none runs with its "edit" flags, logged once. To cap one built-in without redefining it, give only the fields you change: "adapters": { "codex": { "permissions": "read" } }.
//agentEnv: ODW extension. "inherit" (the default) starts agent CLIs with ODW's whole environment. "minimal" passes only PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, LANG, LC_*, TERM, TMPDIR, TZ (and the Windows system variables), the auth and config variables the built-in CLIs document (ANTHROPIC_*, CLAUDE_*, OPENAI_*, CODEX_*, GEMINI_*, GOOGLE_*, DASHSCOPE_*, QWEN_*, MOONSHOT_*, KIMI_*, CURSOR_*, OPENCODE_*, the proxy variables, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS), the adapter's env, ODW_* and the names or globs in "agentEnvPass" (e.g. ["AWS_*"] for Claude Code on Bedrock).
//schemaKeywords: ODW extension. What happens to JSON Schema in an agent()'s schema that ODW's validator does not check. It checks type (one name), enum, properties, required, additionalProperties: false, items (one schema) and minItems; annotations such as description, title and format constrain nothing. Anything else (oneOf/anyOf/allOf, $ref, const, pattern, minimum, maxItems, type unions, …) is never silently unchecked: "warn" (the default) runs the call, validates the rest, and logs once per run which keywords, where, and who enforces them — an adapter whose CLI validates schemas itself ("flags.schema": the built-in claude, and codex for strict schemas), otherwise nobody; "strict" fails the call before it starts, naming each one. A malformed schema (a typo, an unknown type) fails in either mode. A CLI with flags.schema is handed every schema (claude --json-schema, codex --output-schema) and ODW still validates each reply. schemaPrompt "auto" describes the schema in the prompt only for a CLI that does not take it natively; "always" for every CLI.

//notify.$comment: ODW extension: run-end hooks. Rename "//notify" to "notify" to turn them on. They fire once, after the run's final state is written, and can never change it; a failing or slow hook is only logged to the run's worker.log. command: an argv run WITHOUT a shell (killed after 30s), with ODW_RUN_ID, ODW_RUN_STATE, ODW_WORKFLOW, ODW_RUN_DIR, ODW_RESULT_FILE (only when the run has a result), ODW_DURATION_SEC, ODW_AGENTS and ODW_FAILED_AGENTS in its environment. webhook: an http(s) URL that receives a JSON POST (10s limit) whose text/content fields render as-is in Slack and Discord. on: which final states fire them (default: all three).
